results.comment: As usual, Lex is possibly my favorite interviewer.  He asks good questions, doesn’t rush guests, and he connects with a wide variety of people.  Sometimes I‘ve been unimpressed with Elon, but more often I think I’d enjoy being stuck in an elevator, with either of these two—it’d be interesting instead of somewhere between dreary & dreadful! Around 53:45—Lex “Is there a master plan” vs Elon saying there’d be no purpose for a simulation, because a creator would know the outcome:  When I went to college (in Fremont 😎) in the early 80s, for our RN program 92% was the cutoff for an A, 84% for a B, & 76% for a C.  75% & below—a D—failed the program.   People busted their fannies to stay in the program, but it would’ve been hard to argue with the rationale: Patients deserve a nurse who has sufficient grasp of each area to pass both theory & the “practical lab” with a minimum of 75%.  (Certainly they gel together further in a job!) I think we’re here with a purpose, but for there to be a God, the results would have to matter.   I think God knows what we’ll choose, but we don’t.   I think individuals often think enough of themselves—or we rationalize—that the purpose of life is to prove to ourselves who we really are, especially if we stand up for what we believe is right or for core principles—especially when they conflict.  Do we choose Good, Better or Best, or are we content with “So What”, or to take advantage of others?  I tend to think whatever is after this life, there are parameters here, and there, that matter.  Maybe only those with deep integrity will have the full benefit of the best of the next life.  I always thought all the building blocks of our world have intelligence—I agree with Elon that that must be all or nothing.  I was also pleasantly surprised to hear Elon say Israel should aim for extraordinary kindness and that an eye for an eye is a strong perspective in the Middle East!  I’ve been saying it’s hard to expect Do Unto Others and “Go the extra mile” when culturally the whole region’s kept the Abrahamic law of an eye for an eye.   “Commit extraordinary kindness”…. Well verbalized, and he’s right, that’s the only thing that would be a help.   Being a doormat or inviting repeat acts of aggression is not part & parcel of forgiveness.  Forgiveness is about not letting others’ aggression change or sour who you are inside.  A balance IS possible, but the people would have to push Netanyahu.  I don’t think he’ll come to that on his own. “Beating Hatred in the Eternal realm is the hardest boss battle.  In life and in the video game”.   I didn’t expect to rethink Diablo!
